reasoning_traces.think:
The core idea of CARL is to introduce an abstain class into adversarial training, allowing the model to avoid making predictions on inputs that are likely to be adversarial. This is achieved by defining a geometric margin γ(x) which measures how far an input is from the decision boundary. When γ(x) ≤ γ*, the model abstains. The theoretical foundation is provided by Theorem 1, which bounds the adversarial error in terms of the signed-margin CDF F_Γ. The practical implementation uses a combined loss function that includes both standard classification loss and adversarial loss, augmented with a Jacobian regularization term to encourage smooth decision boundaries. This framework enables GSE to implement a no-bet layer that avoids placing bets on inputs deemed adversarial, improving robustness in uncertain environments.
